analysis.problem: Antrenman yapanlar ağırlığı kaydeder ancak hareket formunu, tekrar kalitesini ve gelişimi birlikte takip etmekte zorlanır. Hedef, antrenman sonrası 20 saniyelik notlarla bu boşluğu doldurmaktır.
analysis.turkishAngle: Türk kullanıcı arayüzü, metrik ağırlık birimi ve sade antrenman terimleri kullanılacak. Türkiye talebi bilinmediğinden hipotez yalnızca yerel kullanıcı görüşmeleriyle test edilecek.
features: Antrenman sonrası 20 saniyelik form notu ve tekrar kalitesi seçimi.
Egzersize göre set, ağırlık ve gelişim çizelgesi.
Hareket adı, kısa form ipucu ve sık hata kütüphanesi.
firstCustomers: İstanbul, Ankara ve İzmir'deki 3 bağımsız salonun Instagram hesaplarına doğrudan ulaşarak 10 antrenman yapan kişiden görüşme ve ön sipariş iste.
Antrenman içerikleri paylaşan Türkçe Instagram hesaplarına, takipçilerine yönelik 10 kişilik kısa test grubu öner.
Üniversite spor kulüplerinin WhatsApp topluluklarında 48 saatlik prototip görüşmesi duyur.
validation: İlk 24 saatte 10 hedef kullanıcı bul; en az 5'i form takibini öncelikli sorun olarak doğrulasın.
İkinci 24 saatte 5 kullanıcı prototipi tamamlasın; en az 3'ü 7 günlük kullanıma başlasın.
En az 5 ön sipariş veya depozito alınamazsa teklifi durdur.
Ortalama kayıt süresi 45 saniyenin üzerindeyse akışı sadeleştir veya durdur.
analysis.stopCondition: 48 saatte en az 10 hedef kullanıcıyla görüş. 5 kişi ön sipariş veya depozito vermezse, 3 kullanıcı 7 günlük günlük kullanımı tamamlamazsa veya ortalama kayıt süresi 45 saniyeyi aşarsa dur.
unknowns: Türkiye'de kullanıcı talebi, ödeme isteği ve uygun fiyat bilinmiyor.
Egzersiz ve form içeriklerinin doğruluğu ile güncellenmesi için uzman desteği gerekiyor olabilir.
Mobil mağaza onayı, müşteri edinme maliyeti ve kullanıcı edinim kanalları bilinmiyor.
Kişisel sağlık verisi işlenecekse açık rıza ve veri güvenliği gereksinimleri belirlenmeli.
Rakip yokluğu doğrulanmadı; Krato ve benzeri uygulamalar karşılaştırılmalı.

builder.basis: Dayanak: Krato'nun açıklanan mobil form kütüphanesi, egzersiz takibi ve ciro beyanı; ölçek: tek geliştirici, küçük bir mobil MVP ve ilk 10 kullanıcı. Belirsizlikler: fiyat, Türkiye talebi, içerik doğruluğu, mağaza süreci, müşteri edinme ve rakipler bilinmiyor.

cards.title: Show HN: Mini-AGI – Dynamic continual learning model trained on 8GB VRAM

signals.title: Show HN: Mini-AGI – Dynamic continual learning model trained on 8GB VRAM
signals.description:
Sorry for the pretentious name, I know, I know.. It just contains all the pieces I would like to see a AGI model to have, and I can't stand the temptation. Before throwing rocks at me, please take a glance at the Readme, and I hope it will cover your mood a little bit.

So, first of all it does work and you can see the sample from the whole training run here: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/volotat/mini-AGI/refs/head...

Here is the scaling law graph I have so far, and it looks very promising: https://github.com/volotat/mini-AGI/blob/main/assets/scaling...

The model was built under my deep dissatisfaction so we cannot really train even moderately big models (1B+ scale) on the consumer's hardware. We can inference and fine-tune them for sure, but I would like to have full control over what the model sees over the training run, so it is fully aligned with my interests, not some corporations.

I was thinking about for some time and come up with two interesting ideas I thought worth pursuing: MoE with a lot of experts that gets added and pruned from the model while it trains, where only a small subset of of experts are actually in use at any particular moment + batch 1 training on the single continuous stream of data.

First allows us to be bounded only by the disk space in terms of number of parameters and load and unload experts only when they are needed. The second (if figured out and it turns out to be doable) allows us to get aways with small VRAM capacity because we do not need to store big randomized batches and their respective gradients.

Hi HN!

I wanted to show the world a small project I have been working on, on my spare time, for the past couple of months.

It's a small cross-platform mobile application that works as a dental health tracker. It helps your track really everything (I believe) regarding your dental/oral health.

Features include: - daily reminders to brush your teeth in the morning, after lunch and before bed - a simple 2 minutes brushing timer and a streak counter to see your past brushing habits and get cool insights about your past brushing trends (like at which time of the day you usually brush, what's your most missed day...) - a teeth diagram where you can record your historical teeth conditions so that you never forget about them - a centralized planner for your dentist visits with reminders for your next appointments and a vault to store your documents - a toothbrushes pane where you can manage your active ones and get notified when a manual one or a brush head needs to be replaced (I always forget to do so!), like after 90 days - other minor but cool things like a photo comparer that allows you to compare your smile and if it's becoming whiter, an automatically generated PDF report to share to your dentist and more

I built this because I was looking for something similar for my Android phone, but I wasn't able to find anything cool on the Play Store or something that I could be satisfied with, so I thought why not built it myself this time :)

You can turn on "cloud backups" though to save snapshots of your data to your Google Drive or iCloud on a schedule you can configure, think like how WhatsApp does it.

signals.description:
Fable 5 scored 99.19% on WebVoyager a few months ago, a be A benchmark is not your logged-in admin panel. Browser use agents are no longer demos.

I believe this is a big tipping point.

I have been a web developer for most of my career and building with AI agents for nearly four years. Last October I wrote that the missing piece was browser agents reliable enough to leave alone.

So I published this open source repo, so everyone can have high quality AI employees.

They are, for the most part, agent harness agnostic and can work on any of them.

An AI Employee is a folder of plain text routines that covers one business role: SEO, social, sales, support, web dev, ads, launch work, and a chief of staff that reads the other employees' logs. Eight roles, 60 routines, MIT. They run on your own machine through the agent harness you already use, and they drive your own signed-in browser.

Two of the big things that make my agents better:

- Recursive self improvement reinforcement - Custom trained recipes to get meaningful work done in browser

There's also some other neat features and more planned. Like only-when-needed push notifications for Claude Code and other harnesses that support that.

I'm also building in community recipe and ecosystem contribution. Agents may discover workflows or tricks for high level tasks and contribute them to all other agent operators.

They run a lot of my own business every day now. One example: full meta ad campaigns, content marketing, SEO, backlink building, community management, app development and management.

I recommend you start with one that can take on the work you don't want to do. Or replace yourself.

Happy to answer any questions.

cards.title: Show HN: Bridgeflare – Replace Docker with Cloudflare

signals.title: Show HN: Bridgeflare – Replace Docker with Cloudflare
signals.description:
Hey HN, I have way too many sideprojects so docker images have been eating up most of my RAM, but besides "deploy them" there isn't much I can do during development to cut it down.

So I build Bridgeflare - a drop-in docker replacement that serves the containers on Cloudflare then tunnels them back to you as localhost.

It basically a small daemon that uses the Docker API, so you can just keep using normal docker CLI commands and bridgeflare will do the work underneath:

- Build your image

- Deploy to CF containers

- Setup tunneling across services

- Tunnel them back safely to your machine so you see them as `localhost`

- Small MacOS menu bar to monitor the running containers for ease of use

In a way, it's like the reverse of CF's recently released quick tunnels.

As always, it is early and there are some limits:

- Images need to be amd64 based (CF containers limits)

- No docker exec

- No post-lifecycle persistence

signals.description:
Hi HN!

Laravel has worked with websockets for years but generally speaking it's a one way push architecture (i.e. http in, sockets out).

Lightspeed is kind of like node in that it's a single server that serves your http and your websockets all under one roof. Auth runs in 0.03ms (a Redis read, no database). Your Laravel handler runs inside the full container and the reply comes back down the same socket. I think this could be really cool for creating new ways of working with Laravel.

Anyway, I put together a live demo to show it in action. Basically a cross between slither.io and Asteroids.

Game here:

https://innerloop.works/lightspeed

Repo here:

https://github.com/innerloop-dev/lightspeed

Note: This is 0.1.0, the API may change before 1.0. It needs the Swoole extension and Redis. MIT.

cards.title: Show HN: Pollresults.org – free US election opinion poll API

signals.title: Show HN: Pollresults.org – free US election opinion poll API
signals.description: Not sure if this is even allowed here because of politics, but I made an API for US election poll results. NYT publishes cumulative CSV files with results on their site here (https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/polls/latest-polls.html) under a CC by 4.0 license, so my API parses those files every 10 mins and serves an API from cloudflare. I have done a bunch of random election analytics projects before and this is something I had always wanted.

cards.title: Show HN: Vsqrd – AWS for Biology Experiments

signals.title: Show HN: Vsqrd – AWS for Biology Experiments
signals.description:
Hi hn. We built VSQRD, which is a place to order and run outsourced preclinical studies.

Right now biotechs that outsource studies to CROs (contract research organizations) have to find them manually. That makes it hard to find the right expertise at the right price.

But hey it doesn't have to be this way!! We built vsqrd.com, where CROs can list their study offerings and biotechs can compare and order from them directly. We handle the billing and legal work in the background.

We’re starting with low-stakes non-GLP work like cell viability assays and basic in vitro testing. Over time we want to support the entire outsourcing chain all the way to clinical work.

If you’re a CRO looking to run more studies or a biotech looking to outsource one sign up!

cards.title: Show HN: I wanted Human Benchmark with global leaderboards, so I built it

signals.title: Show HN: I wanted Human Benchmark with global leaderboards, so I built it
signals.description:
Helloooo,

I'm a big fan of cognitive games like Human Benchmark and brain games in general.

I'm also a big fan of Trackmania's leaderboard system, where you can compete globally or by continent, country, region, etc.

So I thought, why not combine the two?

I ended up building Human Rank, a collection of 10 games with global and regional leaderboards.

I'd love to get some feedback and also compete with you guys if you want :)

I'm thinking of creating a discord as well if there are people linking the same things (don't know if it's a good idea tho)

Max.
